first said broswer copy isnt' safe I am always either on work laptio , or phone or etc

the cause, measured, and how I fix it

You are right, and this is the gap. Your planner has kept copies of your items every ten minutes since September — but I measured where they are kept, and they never leave the browser that made them.

your items  → saved to your account  → work laptop · phone · home ✓
your backups → stay in one browser  → invisible from anywhere else ✗

So a bad edit made on your phone syncs everywhere within seconds, while the copy that could undo it sits on a laptop you are not holding. That is your normal situation, not an edge case.

What this adds. One copy a day, saved to your account instead of your browser, kept for 14 days. The planner does it by itself the first time you open it each day — there is nothing to press and nothing to remember.

the copies you have nowwith this card
where keptone browseryour account
visible on your phonenoyes
survives clearing the browserno — goes with the planneryes
how oftenevery 10 minonce a day
cost—free on your current plan

Both are kept. The ten-minute copies stay exactly as they are — they are better for “I just broke something, undo it”. This one is for “I am on a different machine and something is wrong.”

Why it is stored separately, which matters more than it sounds. Your whole planner lives in a single record that is overwritten every time you save. A copy kept inside that record would be overwritten with it — so it would not be a copy at all. Each daily backup gets its own record that your saves never touch.

your planner  → rewritten on every save
backup / 11 Nov  → untouched
backup / 10 Nov  → untouched
backup / 9 Nov   → untouched

It also sidesteps the size limit on the other card: each backup has its own allowance rather than competing with your planner for the same one.

the cause, measured, and how I fix it

Yes — and it is a hard limit you cannot pay to raise. Your whole planner is stored as a single record in your account, and that kind of record is capped at 1,024 KB. I checked rather than assuming: there is no paid tier that lifts it.

████████████████████████  768 KB of 1,024 KB
                     256 KB left

What is filling it, measured from your own data:

whatsizeshare
notes inside tasks649 KB85%
the deleted list52 KB7%
everything else67 KB8%

72 tasks, and the writing inside them is almost all of it. That is not a problem — it is what the planner is for — but it means the number only goes one way.

What happens at 100%. Your account refuses the save. The planner stops syncing and you are stuck on whatever device saved last. There is no warning today: the first you would know is sync failing.

What this card adds: one line in Settings showing how full you are, and a plain warning past 90% saying what to clear. Nothing is deleted and nothing is moved — it only tells you.

The picture shows: ['every number measured from your own 10 Sep data, not estimated', "768 KB compact of a 1,024 KB cap - the cap is the service's, not a setting", '649 KB of it is the notes inside your tasks, across 72 tasks', 'this card only shows you the number - it moves and deletes nothing']

I also thought of — you have not decided this yet

Two things worth saying.

  • This is not urgent, and I am not dressing it up as urgent. At 75% you have room. I am putting it on the board because the failure mode is a silent one — you would find out when syncing broke, which is the worst moment to discover a limit exists.
  • The real fix is bigger, and it is not this card. Eventually each task would be stored on its own instead of all of them together, which removes the ceiling completely. That rewrites how the planner loads and saves everything — the riskiest change there is — and it is not worth doing for a limit that is still 256 KB away. This card buys the warning that tells us when it IS worth doing.

THE RULES OF THIS BOARD — permanent, they never come off

  1. The AFTER shows the SCENARIO you raised, not a tidy example. Added 2026-10-11 in your words: "you need to show me the after picture from those scenarios, always, that is a rule you must adhere by." If you report a control at the bottom of a window, the pictures are OF a control at the bottom of that window — the BEFORE photographed in that exact state, the AFTER showing that same state fixed. A picture of the easy case proves nothing about the case you hit.
  2. EVERY change is drawn here and waits for your word — including a fix to a fix. Restated 2026-10-11 in your words: "from now on, show me on the PNG file before you do anything, then wait for my approval to put it in the demo." I had been treating a correction to something already approved as a continuation of that approval, and putting it straight on the demo. It is not. A new change is a new card, drawn, waiting, however small and however obviously right it looks to me.
  3. Minimax advises; I write the code. Changed 2026-10-11 on your instruction — "change the rules from Minimax from executioner of code to just co-brain only, I feel like a lot of the code stuff you are doing is going back and forth." Every change used to become a written brief, a round-trip and a verification step; on a one-line fix that was four steps, and its own verification was wrong three times in a row. It still advises on every turn — that part earns its place. The gate that enforced the old way is switched off, and kept so it can be switched back.
  4. When you ask to SEE it, you get a photograph of it working — not a drawing, and not the same drawing twice. A drawing is only ever a first look at something not built yet. The moment you ask again, I build it, test it and photograph the real thing. Added 2026-10-10, after I left two drawings on this board across three replies and you had to ask three times.
  5. I do not hand anything back half done. If a card says fixed, it is built, measured, gate-tested and photographed before you read the word. Added 2026-10-10, in your words: "your response must be complete and done before saying done".
  6. I find the pattern before I invent one. Before changing how anything looks, I find the control in the planner that already does that job and copy it. Added 2026-10-10, after I drew a new calendar when the app already had one, and after I changed a css rule that three controls share instead of the one you asked about. Both came from acting on what I expected instead of measuring what is there. When you ask "is that Claude or Minimax" — it is me. Minimax writes only the exact text I dictate.
  7. Your list goes up here first. Every item you raise becomes a card with a BEFORE picture, an AFTER picture and how I would fix it. Nothing is written into the planner before that.
  8. No code before you approve the card. You approve card by card. Only when you say “make it live” do I write anything.
  9. Approved is not live. A card you approve stays here as APPROVED until the build ships, so you can see what is queued.
  10. A card never leaves until you say remove. This board is the record of what you asked for, not a list of what I finished.
  11. Your words are kept, all of them — one line per thing you said. Your first quote stays at the top of the card forever; every later correction is its own dated line underneath, never merged into a paragraph, so you can check each one off. I never replace what you said with my summary.
  12. The AFTER is not one picture — it explains the new setup, step by step, in different pictures. What happens first, what happens next, what it looks like when it works. Never the same picture twice. If nothing is built yet, the card says so in plain words instead of pretending.
  13. Every question sits inside the problem it belongs to — never collected somewhere else. You read one card and answer it there.
  14. I raise what you have not thought of. Every card carries an I also thought of note: the thing your request does not decide — the crowded case, the phone, what happens to what you already have.
  15. I test it in Safari myself — before I call it done, and again after it goes live.
  16. Pictures, not paragraphs. Short words around the picture, never an essay above it.
  17. Every picture is half a page — including the step pictures. The BEFORE and AFTER are half each, and a step picture is the same size, not a thumbnail, because you have to see what is inside it. A shot of the whole browser takes the full width on its own row.
  18. EVERY APPROVED CARD IS SHOWN CONSOLIDATED — folded shut. The moment you approve one it collapses to a single line, so the board only ever shows you what still needs you. Press open beside its number to look at it again. This one is never skipped.
